projects.title: EduShift AI
projects.summary: LMS and business-simulation SaaS at MindShift MENA. Versioned AI simulations with automated competency scoring. One simulation became four production learning products, now used by 6+ organisations.
projects.tagline: An LMS and business-simulation platform that grew from one simulation into four production products.
projects.brief: MindShift MENA runs training programmes that teach decision-making through simulation. The first version was a single hand-built simulation. Each new programme meant a new build. The platform needed to make a simulation a configuration, not a project.
features: Learning management: programmes, cohorts and learner progress
Business simulations that learners play through as decisions with consequences
AI-driven scenarios, versioned so a running cohort is never moved onto a changed prompt
Automated competency scoring against a defined rubric
Configuration instead of code for each new programme

decisions.title: Simulations are versioned, not edited in place
decisions.body: A cohort that started on one version of a simulation finishes on that version. Changing the prompt or the scoring creates a new version, so results within a cohort stay comparable.
decisions.outcome: A cohort's results stay comparable while the product keeps changing.

decisions.title: Scoring is automated against a rubric
decisions.body: Competency scores come from a fixed rubric rather than from a facilitator's reading of each transcript, so two cohorts can be compared on the same scale.
decisions.outcome: Two cohorts are graded on the same scale, without one facilitator's bias.

decisions.title: One engine, many products
decisions.body: The simulation became a configurable engine. That is what let a single simulation turn into four production learning products.
decisions.outcome: A new programme is configuration, not a new build.

projects.stackProse: TypeScript end to end, Next.js on the front, PostgreSQL for data, shipped in Docker containers.

highlights.label: production products grown from one simulation

projects.title: SafeStay
projects.summary: Three-tier platform for verified student housing: a NestJS API, a Next.js console and a Flutter app. Contract signing runs as a server-side state machine, so several parties can sign one contract at different times without it ever being half-signed.
projects.tagline: Verified student housing, where a contract signed by several parties can never be left half-signed.
projects.brief: SafeStay is a platform for verified student housing. One housing contract is signed by several parties, at different times, from two different clients: a Flutter app and a Next.js console. The platform had to keep that contract consistent whichever order the signatures arrive in, and keep the flows behind identity verification.
features: Multi-party contract signing across the Flutter app and the Next.js console
Identity verification (KYC) gating
Scheduled payment reminders, run on the server
One API serving both clients, over a 20+ table schema

decisions.title: The server owns the contract's state
decisions.body: Signing runs as a state machine in the API. Each client renders the current state and asks for a transition; neither client holds the state itself, so the two clients cannot disagree about where a contract stands.
decisions.outcome: A half-signed contract cannot exist in the database.

decisions.title: Verification sits in front of the flows
decisions.body: Identity verification (KYC) gates the platform's flows instead of being a profile badge, so the checks happen before a user can act, not after.
decisions.outcome: Only verified users reach the gated flows.

decisions.title: Reminders are scheduled on the server
decisions.body: Payment reminders run as cron jobs in the API rather than depending on a client being open.
decisions.outcome: Reminders go out whether or not anyone has the app open.

projects.stackProse: NestJS for the API, Next.js for the console, Flutter for the mobile app, and PostgreSQL underneath.

projects.title: AutoBusiness
projects.summary: Freelance build: a bilingual Arabic and English store for courses and templates. Orders move through a server-side state machine under row locks, so approving a payment twice cannot grant access twice.
projects.tagline: A bilingual store for courses and templates, with payment review that cannot grant access twice.
projects.context: Auto Business, a digital-business training brand
projects.brief: The client sells courses and downloadable templates to an Arabic-speaking audience. Card payments were not an option, so buyers pay by InstaPay or Vodafone Cash and upload a receipt. The system had to turn that manual step into something an admin can review safely, in Arabic first, with English as a switch.
features: Arabic-first interface (right to left) with English as a switch, on locale-prefixed routes
Catalogue of courses, templates and bundles priced on their own
Checkout by InstaPay or Vodafone Cash with receipt upload
Admin review queue: approve or reject receipts, with an audit log of every decision
My library: unlocked courses and authenticated file downloads
Two-stage payments for service projects: deposit, then final payment on delivery
Per-page SEO in both languages: hreflang, JSON-LD for courses and products, dynamic sitemap

decisions.title: Orders are a state machine under a row lock
decisions.body: An order moves pending payment, awaiting review, then approved, rejected or cancelled. Every transition runs in one transaction holding a pessimistic write lock. Approving an order twice is a no-op, so a double click or two admins at once cannot grant access twice.
decisions.outcome: A double click, or two admins at once, never gives a course away.

decisions.title: Refresh tokens rotate and detect reuse
decisions.body: Each refresh issues a new token in the same family. If an already-used token comes back, the whole family is revoked. Stored tokens are HMAC-hashed with a purpose prefix, so a reset token can never be replayed as a refresh token.
decisions.outcome: A stolen session token stops working the moment it is replayed.

decisions.title: One service decides access
decisions.body: Bundles expand into per-product entitlements at approval time. A single entitlements service answers every 'can this user see this?' question and supports revocation. Uploads are typed by their magic bytes, not by their file extension.
decisions.outcome: Access rules live in one place, so a new product type cannot leak paid content.

projects.stackProse: A NestJS modular monolith over MariaDB through TypeORM, with a Next.js front end using next-intl for Arabic and English. Zod validates both sides of the contract. Docker runs the full stack locally, including a mail catcher.

highlights.label: Arabic first, English on a switch

projects.title: MSP Tech Club system
projects.summary: Public site and invite-only member system for MSP Tech Club, Capital University. Permission-based RBAC blocks privilege escalation and always keeps one active president. Registration locks the event row, promotes the waitlist and issues QR tickets scanned at the door.
projects.tagline: The public site and member system for a university tech club, with event tickets checked in by QR.
projects.brief: The club ran on a static site and spreadsheets. The board needed invite-only accounts with real roles, events with capacity and a waitlist, and a way to check attendees in at the door, without giving every board member every permission.
features: Public pages: committees, team, media albums and events
Event registration without an account, with a QR ticket sent by email
Capacity limits with an automatic waitlist
Door check-in by scanning the QR ticket from the dashboard
Custom registration forms per event
Invite-only accounts with configurable roles and permissions
Contact inbox, newsletter subscribers and daily reminder emails

decisions.title: Permissions, not role names, guard every route
decisions.body: Routes declare the permission they need. The API refuses to let anyone grant a permission they do not hold, only a President can appoint a President, and the last active President cannot be removed. The club cannot lock itself out.
decisions.outcome: The club cannot lock itself out, and no member can promote themselves.

decisions.title: Registration locks the event row
decisions.body: Each registration runs in a transaction that locks the event. Two people cannot take the last seat. When a seat frees up, the next person on the waitlist is promoted in the same transaction.
decisions.outcome: The last seat is taken once. Nobody is told they are in and then turned away.

decisions.title: Tokens can be revoked
decisions.body: A token version on each user invalidates every issued JWT at once, such as when an account is disabled. Migrations are plain SQL applied at boot and tracked in a table, so a deploy is the whole release process.
decisions.outcome: Disabling an account takes effect at once, on every device.

projects.stackProse: Next.js 15 on the front, NestJS 11 on the API, PostgreSQL on Neon through Drizzle ORM, both deployed on Vercel with a scheduled job for reminders.
